text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Tuesday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- The government will start consideration of the state budget for 1997. The planned income is 7.6 billion litas (22 percent of GDP), planned expenses are 6.359 billion litas and the planned budget deficit is 596 million litas (1.7 percent of GDP). GDP for 1997 is planned at 34.563 billion litas and inflation is forecast to be 16 percent.

- Lithuanian Economy Minister Antanas Kaminskas signed a free trade agreement between the two countries with Czech Industry and Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy in Prague. The bilateral agreement will also help Lithuania to become a member of CEFTA, expected at the end of next year.

- The disputed sea border between Latvia and Lithuania has become a source of tension as Prime Minister Mindaugas Stankevicius does not agree to settle the dispute over the border in the international court.

- The newspaper says in an investigative article that after a period of relative calm, rival mafia gangs are starting to fight to replace the power of the Vilnius Brigade, whose power is one the wane. At present, there are 12 stable criminal groups operating in Vilnius, it says.

- 62 percent of Lithuanian population think that Lithuania's situation has become worse since 1992. Baltijos Tyrimai opinion poll showed that the number of pessimists increased to 85 percent in 1996. The number of people who support the market economy was almost the same as in 1992 at 79 percent. 24 percent of the population thinks that market reforms are too rapid, 45 percent consider them too slow while 24 percent think the pace is right.
- Stankevicius suggested to Latvia that the two nations together start talks with AMOCO on the exploration area in the disputed sea area.

- Polish Kredyt bank is likely to be the first foreign bank in Lithuania. Kredyt Bank officials signed a letter of intent to buy the former Litimpeks Bank building. The newspaper's sources say the deal is worth three million litas.
- The foreign ministry considers the ratification by the Latvian parliament of the oil deal with Amoco to be a violation of Lithuania's sovereign rights.
